messages.subject: The first topic
messages.body_plain:
When we created the lavaan.org <http://lavaan.org> website, we envisioned that sooner or later, the website would host a user-based forum. For several reasons, this never happened. In the next coming months, we plan to redesign lavaan.org <http://lavaan.org>. In those new plans, there is no room anymore for a website-based forum. Instead, I will try to divert all questions and discussions about lavaan to this discussion group. For bug reports, please report an issue at github (https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues).

Yves.
http://lavaan.org

Thank you,

messages.body_plain:
On 09/14/2012 04:40 PM, Renï¿½ wrote:
> Dear lavaan-group,
>
> I'm trying to run a multigroup-CFA with effects-coding, e.g. for each
> construct constrain the factor loadings of the measured indicators to
> average to one (like suggested by Card & Little In Studying Aggression
> with Structural Equation Modeling ). But it ends up beeing singular.
> What has to be changed to make this work?
>
>
> library(lavaan)
>
> HS.model <- '
> visual   =~ c(l11,l11)*x1 + c(l21,l21)*x2 + c(l31,l31)*x3
> textual  =~ c(l12,l12)*x4 + c(l22,l22)*x5 + c(l32,l32)*x6
> speed   =~ c(l13,l13)*x4 + c(l23,l23)*x5 + c(l33,l33)*x6
>
> l11 == 3 - l21 - l31
> l12 == 3 - l22 - l32
> l13 == 3 - l23 - l33'
>
> fit <-
> lavaan( model = HS.model,
> data = HolzingerSwineford1939,
> auto.var = TRUE,
> auto.fix.first = FALSE,
> group = "school" ,
> group.equal = c("loadings")
> )
>
>
> Error in solve.default(E) :

Several things. First, for the 'speed' factor, the indicators are x7, x8
and x9 (not x4, x5 and x6). Second, you are using the lavaan() function.
This means you need to specify _all_ the parameters, either in the
syntax, or by using various auto.* and other flags). You forgot the
intercepts of the observed variables, and the covariances among the
exogenous latent variables:

HS.model <- '
visual  =~ c(l11,l11)*x1 + c(l21,l21)*x2 + c(l31,l31)*x3
textual =~ c(l12,l12)*x4 + c(l22,l22)*x5 + c(l32,l32)*x6

speed   =~ c(l13,l13)*x7 + c(l23,l23)*x8 + c(l33,l33)*x9

l11 == 3 - l21 - l31
l12 == 3 - l22 - l32
l13 == 3 - l23 - l33'

fit <- lavaan(model = HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939,

               auto.var = TRUE, auto.fix.first = FALSE,

               group = "school", auto.cov.lv.x = TRUE,
               int.ov.free = TRUE)

 > fit
lavaan (0.5-10) converged normally after 354 iterations

   Number of observations per group
   Pasteur                                          156
   Grant-White                                      145

   Estimator                                         ML
   Minimum Function Chi-square                  124.044
   Degrees of freedom                                54
   P-value                                        0.000

Chi-square for each group:

   Pasteur                                       68.824
   Grant-White                                   55.219

Hope this helps,

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: cfa output
messages.body_plain:
On 09/14/2012 02:44 PM, fabio alexander sierra matamoros wrote:
> Dear Lavaan users
>
> I have run lavaan with ordinal data because we are validating a quality
> of life scale. I would like to know the variances of each item (observed
> variable) and what is the meaning of the thresholds reported in the
> fit.measures output.

Do you mean the residual variances? They are indeed not (yet) reported
by lavaan, since they are not free parameters. The residual variances of
the indicators are a function of the other parameters. One way to
compute them (at least using 0.5-9) is as follows (assuming 'fit'
contains the fitted object):

1 - diag(fitted(fit)$cov)

or more neatly:

round(1 - diag(fitted(fit)$cov), 3)

As for the meaning of the thresholds, they estimate the 'cut-off' values
used to get from the (continuous) latent response variable to the
observed ordered categories. See for example this reference for a
discussion of thresholds:

Anders Skrondal1 and Sophia Rabe-Hesketh (2005). Structural Equation
Modeling: Categorical Variables. Entry for the Encyclopedia of
Statistics in Behavioral Science, Wiley, 2005.

(available as http://www.gllamm.org/SEMcat.pdf)

Yves.

An automatic way to draw CFA's from lavaan with R comes with the
psych-package by Revelle.
The following is from his lesson 'Psychology 454: Latent Variable
Modeling', see slide 28 from
http://personality-project.org/revelle/syllabi/454/wk6.lavaan.pdf.

library(psych)
library(lavaan)
b2 <- Bechtoldt.2[c(3:8,15:17),c(3:8,15:17)]
Thurstone.mod <- ' F1 =~ Sentences + Vocabulary + Completion
             F2 =~ First_Letters + Four_letter_words + Suffixes
             F3 =~ Letter_Series + Pedigrees + Letter_Grouping'

t.cfa.2 <- cfa(Thurstone.mod,sample.cov=b2,sample.nobs=213,std.lv <http://std.lv>=TRUE)
summary(t.cfa.2)

lavaan.diagram <-
function(fit,model="cfa",...) {
                 if(model=="cfa") {
                           fx=fit@Model@GLIST$lambda
                           colnames(fx) <- fit@Model@dimNames$lambda[[2]]
                           Phi <- fit@Model@GLIST$psi
                           Rx <- fit@Model@GLIST$theta
                           v.labels <- fit@Model@dimNames$lambda[[1]]

structure.diagram(fx=fx,Phi=Phi,Rx=Rx,labels=v.labels,...)
                 } else
{structure.diagram(fx=fit@Model@GLIST$lambda,Phi=fit@Model@GLIST$beta,
Rx=fit@Model@GLIST$theta,...) }
}
lavaan.diagram(t.cfa.2)

Alternativly if one wishes to plot with R, one needs to call RGraphviz
or qplot and build up all from the skretch.

regards,
Ren�

It is due to the version number of lavaan (0.4-14). Please update to the
newest version (0.5-9), where we have changed the way standard errors
are computed in the presence of constraints.

The error in the 0.4-14 was due to the fact that the 'expected
information matrix' (called E in lavaan), was not of full rank, and
could not be inverted.

(I also see now that we don't need to specify the group.equal= argument
in the lavaan call, since the loadings have been fixed already in the
syntax).

Yves.

messages.subject_clean: How to free a labelled parameter
messages.body_plain:
Here is a univariate ALT model (eg. Bollen and Curran, 2006)

model <-  ' i =~ lambda11*y11 + 1*y12 + 1*y13 + 1*y14
                s =~ lambda12*y11 + 1*y12 + 2*y13 + 3*y14
               y12 ~ rho*y11
               y13 ~ rho*y12
               y14 ~ rho*y13
               lambda11 == 1/(1-rho)
               lambda12 == -rho/(1-rho)^2 '

The loadings of the first indicators are labelled so they can be referred to in the model constraints. But I also want them to be free parameters under the model constraints.
I can't set std.lv <http://std.lv> because I don't want to fix the factor variances.How shall I free the loadings of the first indicators?

best wishes.

> shall I free the loadings of the first indicators?

You can list an indicator more than once, each time with a different
'modifier', for example:

i =~ lambda11*y11 + NA*y11 + 1*y12 + 1*y13 + 1*y14

y11 occurs two times on the right hand side of the =~ operator, once for
the label, and once with 'NA' modifier; the latter will force the
parameter to be free

Or you can use the lavaan() function, and use the auto.* flags at will.

Yves.

messages.body_plain:
On 09/19/2012 06:39 PM, fabio presaghi wrote:
> Hi,
> I'm testing a multiple-group cfa model (two independent sample) and my
> main objective is to test the invariance of the model across the two
> samples. Is it possible with lavaan to perform an omnibus test of

> covariance matrices  (i.e., Σg = Σg′) as suggested byVandenberg, &

> Lance, (2000, pp. 12, option (a)) ?
> Thank you
>
> References
> Vandenberg, & Lance, (2000). A review and synthesis of the measurement
> invariance literature: Suggestions, practices, and recommendations for

> organizational research. /Organizational Research Methods/, 2, 4-69.

This is simply Box's M test for equal covariances, right? There is no
canned function to do just this in lavaan (maybe in other packages?). Of
course, you could do it manually: specify a model with only variances
and covariances, and constrain them to be equal across groups. For the
Holzinger & Swineford model, this would be something like:

HS.model.BOX.M <- ' x1 ~~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
                     x2 ~~ x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
                     x3 ~~ x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
                     x4 ~~ x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
                     x5 ~~ x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
                     x6 ~~ x6 + x7 + x8 + x9
                     x7 ~~ x7 + x8 + x9
                     x8 ~~ x8 + x9
                     x9 ~~ x9
                   '

fit <- cfa(HS.model.BOX.M, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, group="school",
            meanstructure=FALSE,
            group.equal=c("residuals", "residual.covariances"))
summary(fit)

(the terms 'residuals' and 'residual.covariances' in the group.equal
argument seem a bit odd here; I may provide the aliases 'ov.variances'
and 'ov.covariances' in a future release)

Yves.

On 09/22/2012 07:47 PM, mike wrote:
> In a latent difference score model (McArdle and Hamagami, 2001) the
> latent true score and latent difference score variances are set to 0.
> But the following snip from a model doesn't achieve this and sets them
> to 1 instead:
>      ly1 ~~ 0*ly1

Hm. This is either a bug, or another piece of syntax is overriding this.
This syntax should fix the variance of 'ly1' to zero. Could you provide
me with the complete syntax and perhaps a snippet of the data so that we
can reproduce this?

> By the way can we have a "..." argument in "growth" to pass options
> through to lavaan?

That would not be trivial, since growth() currently adds (and sets)
several auto.* arguments. If one of these is also passed through the
'...' argument, we may end up with duplicated arguments.

The growth() function is really only for simple growth models. I do
think it should be possible to have a custom function for latent
difference models (and only those). For everything else, we need the
lavaan() function.

Yves.

messages.body_plain:
Dear Yves,
thanks for your help and your work on this great package.
Below is the model syntax. Its a univariate dual change score LDS model. For a path diagram of this see figure 7a in:
McArdle (2009). Annual Review of Psychology, 60:577–605
For data I just used the Mplus example "ex6.1.dat", naming the variables: y1, y2, y3, y4. I run it like this:
summary(growth(model, data))
For the variances of ly1-ly4 and dy1-dy3 I get 1 instead of 0.

model =  "# Latent true scores
          ly1 =~ 1*y1
          ly2 =~ 1*y2
          ly3 =~ 1*y3
          ly4 =~ 1*y4
          # Autoregressions
          ly2 ~ 1*ly1
          ly3 ~ 1*ly2
          ly4 ~ 1*ly3
          # Latent difference scores
          dy1 =~ 1*ly2
          dy2 =~ 1*ly3
          dy3 =~ 1*ly4
          # Proportional Change
          dy1 ~ beta*ly1
          dy2 ~ beta*ly2
          dy3 ~ beta*ly3
          # Slope (sy) and level (y0)
          sy =~ 1*dy1
          sy =~ 1*dy2
          sy =~ 1*dy3
          y0 =~ 1*ly1
          # Free means and variances
          y0 ~ 1
          sy ~ 1
          y0 ~~ y0
          sy ~~ sy
          # Observed means
          y1 ~ 0*1
          y2 ~ 0*1
          y3 ~ 0*1
          y4 ~ 0*1
          # Fix latent means at 0
          ly1 ~ 0*1
          ly2 ~ 0*1
          ly3 ~ 0*1
          ly4 ~ 0*1
          dy1 ~ 0*1
          dy2 ~ 0*1
          dy3 ~ 0*1
          # Fix latent variance at 0
          ly1 ~~ 0*ly1       ############ HERE IS MY PROBLEM
          ly2 ~~ 0*ly2       # For some reason this sets the variances to 1
          ly3 ~~ 0*ly3       # I could make it work with something like: ly3 ~~ 0.0001*ly3
          ly4 ~~ 0*ly4       # Or better: ly4 ~~ omega*ly4
          dy1 ~~ 0*dy1       # and then:  omega == 0
          dy2 ~~ 0*dy2
          dy3 ~~ 0*dy3
          # Equality constraints on residuals
          y1 ~~ e*y1
          y2 ~~ e*y2
          y3 ~~ e*y3
          y4 ~~ e*y4"

best wishes, Mike

messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike,

The idea of programming simple functions to help create complex models is one of the reasons I love R. If, you or someone else was interested in creating a function to generate lavaan syntax/parameter tables for complex but common models (like the LDS model), I believe we have a home for it. In collaboration with some colleagues, we've written an R package for miscellaneous but helpful functions related to SEM. The package name is semTools, and the goal of the package is for it to include contributions from anyone who is interested in writing functions. We would certainly love to have functions that make specifying LDS models in there!

Thanks,

-Alex

This is a bug in 0.5-9, but has already been fixed in 0.5-10. It only
occurs if you have an empty cell in one of the pairwise tables. To
install the dev version, type in R:

install.packages("lavaan", repos="http://www.da.ugent.be", type="source")

If you still get this error (or if you have any other issues), let me know.

Yves.
